summary.intent: Triage and fix CodeRabbit CLI findings on the Phase 67/68 diff, deferring non-trivial or pre-existing issues as tracked todos.
summary.outcome: 5 of 16 findings fixed (NaN epoch guard, epoch integer guard, 2 new tests, ROADMAP counter, STATE.md drift); 9 deferred as 3 todo files; 1 dismissed as false positive; 1 skipped as historical record. All affected test suites green (76 passed in tee-worker, 9 in sdk-core).

repo: ROADMAP.md can drift from actual plan completion state — '7/8' was showing while all 8 plans were marked [x] and phase 67-08 was done.
STATE.md has two sources of truth for phase/progress: YAML frontmatter (stayed accurate) and human-readable 'Current focus' + progress bar (drifted to stale Phase 67 / 0-of-9 values).
CodeRabbit finding on `parsed.value` round-trip `toBe` comparison is a false positive — the value is a string, so primitive equality holds across separately-parsed records.

code.finding: Missing NaN guard on epoch input; added validation to reject NaN before downstream use.
Epoch validation only checked non-finite; tightened to also reject non-integer and negative values.
Added 2 tests for malformed-anchor / NaN-epoch edge cases in getInternalCurrentEpoch, raising suite to 76 tests.

workflow: CodeRabbit CLI exits 0 even with findings; exit code alone does not signal a clean review.
Triage order: verify each finding against live code before fixing — several were pre-existing naming issues or guaranteed-by-construction and would have been wasted effort to fix.
Grouping deferred findings into thematic todo files (error-handling, naming, invariant coverage) is cleaner than one-todo-per-finding when items share a fix context.

friction: STATE.md human-readable section silently drifted from frontmatter — a known recurring regression requiring manual correction after each phase.

CodeRabbit produced 16 findings requiring per-item code verification before any fix, with a mix of real bugs, false positives, pre-existing issues, and design-level concerns that cannot be resolved mechanically.
